title: Resolve KV-handoff livelock causing multi-tenant queue starvation and long-context tail
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sustained p99/p999 tail latency increases and intermittent API errors. Rooted in a rare scheduler livelock during KV-cache handoff and dequeue ordering under mixed short/very-long context workloads, causing queue starvation for latency-sensitive tenants.
background: Over the past three weeks we've seen repeat escalations from three customers (Hosted-Public API, Dedicated-cluster A, Private-onprem customer X) where the platform briefly stops serving low-latency requests while long-context requests dominate GPU streams. Alerts triggered by latency SLO breaches and token-rate deviations. Several existing fixes for adaptive batching reduced but did not eliminate these events. This issue differs from previous 'head-of-line' bugs because it manifests only when KV cache eviction aligns with scheduler preemption windows, producing a livelock between the dispatcher and worker handoff logic.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate mixed workload with tenants A (short prompts, high QPS) and B (infrequent >32k tokens continuations).
2) Enable continuous-batching with adaptive_floodgate and enable_kv_prefetch=true in runtime config.
3) Drive a sudden microburst of long-context requests to saturate KV cache and trigger eviction while short-requests are enqueued.
4) Observe worker threads repeatedly yielding during KV handoff; dispatcher backoff increments but failing to drain priority_short queue, producing p99 spike and 429s for short-tenant.
5) Capture scheduler traces and worker flame graphs (attached in related_links) to reproduce livelock.
Note: requires deterministic seed harness used in QA harness/long-tail-sim (see related_links).
root_cause: A race between the KV eviction/handoff path and the scheduler's preemptive dequeue logic. When eviction path holds the worker lock while performing multi-shard KV operations, dispatcher preemption timers intersect and the worker yields without enqueueing pending short-requests, repeatedly reacquiring the worker with a different token set. This sequence forms a livelock: long requests make progress but never commit cache state fast enough to allow short-requests to be routed to idle execution lanes, amplifying backlog and producing queue starvation.
fix_summary: Primary fix: introduce bounded handoff window and cooperative yield point during KV operations; add fast-path bypass for latency-sensitive short requests so they can be routed to warm workers even if full KV handoff is pending. Also add preemption accounting to the dispatcher to avoid repeated yield-reacquire cycles. Secondary fixes: improved metrics, additional locks' timeouts, and safety fallback to force dispatch when short-queue depth > threshold.
code_changes: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7214 - tests: long-tail-sim deterministic harness and regression cases
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs to canary branch and run full CI + long-tail-sim suite on x86+NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI250 ephemeral QA clusters (2 days).
2) Canary rollout to 3 Hosted clusters with telemetry flags enabled for preemption_accounting and handoff_timeout (48h), monitor p50/p95/p99 and token-throughput.
3) Gradual promotion to Dedicated pools with controlled tenant selection (customers consenting to early patch) and Private customers via upgrade bundle (patch notes & runbook).
4) If regressions found, auto-revert via release manager and open follow-up hotfix (fast rollback path documented).
5) Full rollout after 7 days of stable canary metrics and sign-off from Reliability and Product on customer impact reduction.
test_plan: - Unit tests for scheduler handoff boundary conditions (added 12 tests)
- Integration long-tail-sim: deterministic seed harness to reproduce livelock (run in CI nightly)
- Chaos test: inject artificial KV latency and worker preemption at random points to verify no queue starvation
- Performance regression: benchmark p50/p95/p99 across mixed short/long workloads pre/post patch with same seed
- Staging soak: 72h soak with production-like traffic generator per region
monitoring_queries: - Query: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM requests WHERE scheduler_event='handoff' BY deployment
- Dashboards: add 'kv_handoff_livelock' visualization and annotate deploy windows
- SLI: % of short-requests served within 200ms; target >= 99.5%
customer_reports: Hosted: Customer HID-091 (AI-saas) reported 15-minute p99 spike and 1200 429s on 2026-02-24; debug traces attached.
Dedicated: Customer DED-ALPHA cluster experienced periodic latency regressions during batch migrations on 2026-02-27.
Private: Onprem Customer X filed escalation 8472 and had to toggle routing-policy to fallback model to regain low-latency paths.
dependencies: infra-ops: need ephemeral QA GPUs scheduled (req #QA-342)
sdk-team: minor client-side retry change to honor server-side 429->retry-after mapping
notes: We intentionally keep the handoff-timeout conservative to avoid state corruption under Private/offline upgrade scenarios. Design doc for the cooperative handoff is in related_links. Notify customers with scheduled Dedicated or Private upgrades about potential short maintenance window when applying upgrade bundle. Follow-up ticket planned to explore auto-scaling heuristics that proactively prevent KV eviction storms.
